 Melbourne Renegades Women have won their previous match against Hobart Hurricanes Women by 4 wickets.

Heather Graham also lost her wicket when it mattered the most. It was Nicola Carey, who then took the responsibility of taking Hobart Hurricanes to a respectable total. She made 62 runs in 43 balls and got great support from Chinelle Henry, who scored a quickfire 36 to help Hobart Hurricanes Women get past the 150 run mark, and they finished at 154 in 20 overs of play.
 During the chase, Olivia Porter and Hayley Matthews started off very well, adding 32 quick runs for the 1st wicket partnership. Porter got out after scoring 14 runs while Hayley Matthews went on to make 59 runs in 44 balls. Courtney Webb also contributed healthily, scoring 29 runs and Melbourne Renegades Women managed to chase the target down in the last over with 4 wickets in hand.

 Adelaide Strikers Women have lost their previous match against Brisbane Heat Women by 14 runs.
 Brisbane Heat Women batted first and they posted a total of 184 for 4 in 20 overs. Grace Harris and Charli Knott started off very well. They collected 57 runs for the 1st wicket partnership. Harris got out for 22 while Knott played shots to all parts of the ground and scored 104 runs in 61 deliveries, hitting 12 fours and 4 sixes. Yastika Bhatia, Annie O'Neil and Orla Prendergast also contributed well to help Brisbane Heat Women get to a very competitive total of 184 in 20 overs of play.
 During the chase, Adelaide Strikers Women lost the key wickets of Maia Bouchier and Tahlia McGrath quite early into the innings. After their dismissals, Laura Wolvaardt and Madeline Penna played to their potential and made 75 and 68 runs respectively. Wolvaardt consumed only 48 deliveries for her knock of 75 while Penna took 45 balls. At this point of time, Adelaide Strikers Women looked like they would cruise home quire comfortably. However, Laura's dismissal slowed things down. Bridget Patterson and Ellie Johnston couldn't play according to the situation. They wasted too many deliveries and Adelaide Strikers Women were eventually restricted to 170 for 5 in 20 overs, losing the match by 14 runs.
